question.text: Mr. Ramesh Iyer, CFO at Himalaya Arbitrage Fund (a Category III AIF structured as an irrevocable determinate trust), is briefing a new analyst on the fund's tax framework. He states that a specific ITA section which grants pass-through status to Category I and II AIFs does NOT apply to Category III AIFs. Which section is he referring to?

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 115UB (read with Section 10(23FBA)/10(23FBB)) grants pass-through treatment to Category I and II AIFs. Under the ITA, no pass-through status has been accorded to a Category III AIF — it is taxed at the fund level under general trust taxation principles (typically MMR under Section 161(1A) or 164). Section 112A deals with LTCG on listed equity; Section 10(38) was the old LTCG exemption (withdrawn 2018); Section 80C is an individual deduction. The Trap: Candidates who remember Section 115UB as the 'AIF tax section' forget that it applies only to Cat I/II. Options B–D are other popular ITA sections used as plausible distractors, but they govern unrelated topics. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-D (Cat I/II Managers) treats Section 115UB pass-through as the primary tax regime. XIX-E (here) deliberately excludes it — pass-through does NOT apply to Cat III. XIX-B (Cat III Distributors) also tests this contrast from the client-communication angle. Manager's Pro-Tip: Budget at fund level. Because Section 115UB is unavailable, every rupee of business income at Himalaya Arbitrage is hit at MMR (~42.744%) BEFORE distribution — so a 15% gross strategy only delivers ~8.6% net to LPs. Build tax drag into hurdle-rate and HWM math, and never quote gross returns to LPs without the fund-level tax haircut.
